reconcile.connective: JFB argues the "chains" describe Satan's final doom, already decreed but not yet executed, leaving him free to roam in the meantime.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible sets 2 Peter 2:4 and Jude 6's chained angels against Job's and 1 Peter 5:8's roaming devil as a contradiction.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Is the devil tied up or free to roam?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/devil_free.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/devil_free.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Not inconsistent with Pe1 5:8; for though their final doom is hell, yet for a time they are permitted to roam beyond it in "the darkness of this world." Slaves of Tartarus (called "the abyss," or "deep," Luk 8:31; "the bottomless pit," Rev 9:11) may also come upon earth. Step by step they are given to Tartarus, until at last they shall be wholly bound to it.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: JFB explicitly denies inconsistency between 2 Peter 2:4's chains and 1 Peter 5:8's roaming devil, resolving it via a final doom decreed but only gradually executed.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871)
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treats this exact tension at both 1 Peter 5:8 and 2 Peter 2:4, arguing the chains name Satan's final doom rather than his present confinement.

link.title: 2 Peter 2:4—Are fallen angels bound or are they free to tempt human beings?
link.note: live apologetic treatment arguing the chains describe fallen angels' decreed destiny, not their present status
